_note: Admission cards for gates BORN AFTER 2026-08-23. Read by hooks/gate-edit-gate.py, which refuses a NEW blocking gate whose card is absent or incomplete. A matcher that only announces needs no card: this prices the power to refuse work, never the work of building a check.
_why: The 2026-08-23 gates-audit council (out/council/gates-audit-20260823/) found the system running 59 named controls, born one reasonable afternoon at a time, with gate-edit re-blessing hashes and nothing anywhere asking whether the next control should be able to stop a session. Grok's chair, high confidence: 'This is the missing gate that prevents the next 59 from becoming 90.'
_grandfathered: Every gate already in ops/config/gate-baseline.json on 2026-08-23 keeps its place with no card. That is deliberate, not an oversight: a check that failed on day one across forty-odd existing gates would be muted on day one, which is the failure ops/enforcement-coverage-check.py documents at length and answers the same way. The debt is real and belongs to the telemetry sentence the same council ordered, not to a wall in front of today's work.

_questions.parent_incident: the dated incident where prose failed. Either this or landing_harm is required; a recitation of a taught rule is not parentage.
_questions.landing_harm: one sentence: if this does not bind, WHICH artifact lands in WHOSE hands. 'Could be bad' does not qualify.
_questions.bind_moment: the last cheap reversible moment before that harm. A true rule at the wrong moment is a tax.
_questions.consumer: who receives the wrong artifact. If the only consumer is the gate's own log, the gate is sediment.
_questions.self_serve_remedy: what a refused session can DO, without a new login. A dead end fails even when the rule is right.
_questions.scarce_resource_cost: what it spends, in order of scarcity: Joe's and Dell's attention, this Mac's wall-clock under parallel sessions, Stop-reopen tokens, billed CI minutes.
_questions.unique_bind: why nothing already binds this class at this moment. Two blockers on one claim-set fail uniqueness.
_questions.matcher_test: a repo-relative fixture path that EXISTS, written before the gate (rule e65efc68). A card naming a test nobody wrote is the box-ticking version of this control.

context-handoff-gate.py.parent_incident: On 2026-08-30 transcript a8e1daa6-3c72-4334-9d13-f52f4a9be88e crossed 1,013,084 tokens, auto-compacted to 38,496, and the later Stop invocation silently allowed because it saw only postcompact usage.
context-handoff-gate.py.landing_harm: Without a verified successor receipt, a source task can compact or terminate while its unfinished repository ownership, decisions, and exact next action exist on no active surface.
context-handoff-gate.py.bind_moment: The Stop boundary after the configured soft or hard threshold, while the source task can still complete a same-task ownership transfer.
context-handoff-gate.py.consumer: The successor task and dispatcher that must continue the same CARR System OS slice without duplicate or missing ownership.
context-handoff-gate.py.self_serve_remedy: Create and pin a same-slice successor, write and read back the immutable offer/receipt/final evidence through this gate's CLI, then retry Stop after TAKEOVER_VERIFIED.
context-handoff-gate.py.scarce_resource_cost: One reopened model turn only after a measured threshold or conservative fallback cap; PostToolUse notices are one-shot and PreCompact never blocks.
context-handoff-gate.py.unique_bind: No other gate preserves precompact high-water, validates cross-surface ownership receipts, or refuses Stop until the successor takeover is verified.
